title: Uniform global cellwise Lipschitz bounds and bounded local supports on finite positive balanced embedded complexes
status: FULL new ROOT working argument, UNREVIEWED
ordinary_foundations: Real completeness, finite-dimensional compactness/linear algebra, elementary convex secants, nearest-point first variation and polyhedral divergence theorem, all as disclosed by WHOLE S291; additional steps reconstructed in full here.

units.statement: Precise new working assertion and inherited convexity.
units.proof:
Let X be the support of a finite pure d-dimensional rational polyhedral complex in a fixed Euclidean lattice space, d>=1, with strictly positive actual REAL top weights balanced at every facet. There is no omitted boundary equation. Fix one finite rational common refinement on which a continuous REAL PA function gamma is affine on every cell. Its maximum minimal-Euclidean-extension gradient norm is G<infinity. Let f be continuous printed-PC, testing rational endpoints with actual real nonnegative barycentric weights and face incidences, and |f-gamma|<=C globally. The new assertion is: there are finite geometry constants A_X,B_X, independent of f,C,G, such that f on EVERY fixed convex cell is globally (A_X C+B_X G)-Lipschitz in that cell's Euclidean metric. At every point of every face there is a local ambient supporting form of uniformly bounded norm, supporting f on all cells incident to that face. This is a cellwise and intrinsic-path estimate. It is NOT an assertion of ambient-metric Lipschitzness between arbitrary points on disjoint or distant nonincident cells, whose references can have different recession slopes.

The WHOLE mathematically accepted S291, with BOTH source and reader clarification records, is an explicit conditional input; native218 original-source/combined FAIL and historical INCONCLUSIVE remain. Its local positive-star-spanning and continuous real-endpoint PCC arguments apply to relatively open embedding charts of this positive balanced support. The compact maximum/global-envelope conclusions are not applied to a noncompact space. For clarity we reconstruct their decisive local mechanisms below; every remaining distance, derivative, induction and quantitative step is new working proof, not an imported unreviewed label.

Continuous printed-PC implies convexity on EACH inherited convex cell sigma without coarsening. Given real endpoints in sigma, their barycenter has a minimal rational complex face tau contained in sigma. Put the endpoints in that same assigned cell. In perspective variables t_j=alpha_j x_j the equations sum alpha=1, alpha>=0, each endpoint-cell inequality A_j t_j>=alpha_j b_j and sum t_j in tau are rational linear constraints. Delete zero weights and approximate inside the actual minimal feasible face by rational particular solutions/kernel coordinates, preserving inactive strict slacks. Their endpoints t_j/alpha_j and centers are rational and their PCC is legal. Continuity passes to the original real combination. Thus the ordinary convex inequality holds on the whole sigma and all its faces. This also proves all real-endpoint PCC tests used below, retaining the actual inherited cells.

units.statement: Uniform distance to a nonempty polyhedral inset, proved from nearest points.
units.proof:
For a nonempty closed polyhedron P={x:n_j.x<=b_j} in its own finite-dimensional affine hull, define delta(x)=max(0,max_j(n_j.x-b_j)). There is a finite H_P with dist(x,P)<=H_P delta(x) for ALL x in that affine hull. Let z be a nearest point and w=x-z. The outward normal cone at z is generated by the active n_j. To prove this directly, that finitely generated cone is closed by eliminating dependent nonnegative active columns until an independent subset remains; the finite inverse-column maps bound its coefficients on bounded represented sets. If w were outside the cone, nearest-point separation supplies v with n_j.v<=0 on every active row and w.v>0. Every inactive row has strict slack, so z+t v belongs to P for small t>0. Squared-distance differentiation contradicts nearestness. Hence w=sum_active lambda_j n_j, lambda_j>=0. Dependence elimination again gives an independent surviving subset and sum lambda_j<=H_P||w|| with one constant for all finitely many subsets. Since n_j.z=b_j on that subset,
||w||^2=sum lambda_j(n_j.x-b_j)<=delta(x) sum lambda_j<=H_P delta(x)||w||.
Cancel ||w||, or use the trivial w=0 case. Equalities are removed by working in the relative affine hull; zero normals are harmless. This is an elementary proof, not a Hoffman theorem imported by name.

For a complex face tau, list its own facet inequalities and ALL inequalities of ALL incident top cells sigma whose restrictions are strictly positive in ri(tau); inequalities vanishing identically on tau are not in this list. Choose one rational z0 in ri(tau). All finitely many listed slacks are positive there, so choose rational delta_tau>0 below their minimum. Strengthen the listed inequalities by delta_tau and keep the original remaining inequalities of tau. The resulting relative polyhedron tau_delta is nonempty. At ANY y in tau, the maximal violation of this strengthened system is at most delta_tau. The preceding bound gives a nearest z=z_tau(y) in tau_delta with ||z-y||<=D_tau=H_tau_delta delta_tau, uniformly even when y tends to infinity or to the boundary. If the list is empty use tau_delta=tau and D_tau=0. For dim tau=0, z=y and D_tau=0. This inset step replaces the nonuniform choice of one fixed interior anchor on an unbounded face.

units.statement: Fixed finite star generators span the whole local tangent span.
units.proof:
For y in ri(tau), every incident top cell has the SAME rational tangent cone C_sigma(tau), independent of y. Its lineality is T_tau=span(tau-tau). Choose finite rational conic generators, including both signs of a rational basis of T_tau, and assign every generator v_j to one incident sigma_j. Let E_tau be the linear span of the union of these cones. Their conical hull is E_tau. Here is the positive-balancing reason. Give each top cone Euclidean density equal to its actual positive weight times saturated tangent-lattice covolume. A primitive quotient normal projects to (cell covolume/facet covolume) times its inward unit conormal; balancing therefore cancels all internal facet fluxes with these densities. If a nonzero linear form ell were nonnegative on the entire star and strictly positive somewhere in E_tau, apply the divergence theorem cone by cone in the unit ball to the tangent projection of its constant ambient gradient. Its divergence is zero and internal facets cancel. Outer spherical flux is the weighted nonnegative angular integral of ell, strictly positive on an open patch of some top cone by purity and positive weights. This contradiction excludes a proper supporting halfspace. A finite generated cone is closed by the independent-column argument of L1, and nearest-point separation from a point outside it would supply such a halfspace. Hence it is the entire span. Dimension-one flux is the same endpoint cancellation. This is the whole S291 local star argument with its explicit real-weight covolume convention; no boundary or abstract cellwise-only chart is inserted.

Consequently EVERY v in E_tau has a nonnegative representation by this one finite generator list with total coefficient <=K_tau||v||. Eliminate dependent active columns until an independent subset remains and use the maximum of the finitely many inverse-column bounds. In particular this works for both v and -v. It is stronger than simply having one zero-sum positive relation; the uniform coefficient bound is needed below.

units.statement: Uniform local supports on ri(tau), conditional only on a global face Lipschitz bound.
units.proof:
Suppose f|tau is globally M_tau-Lipschitz; for a point face put M_tau=0. Keep the finite star generators from L2. Choose epsilon_tau>0 small enough that z+epsilon_tau v_j belongs to its assigned sigma_j for EVERY z in tau_delta and every j. This choice is uniform: each inactive sigma inequality has slack >=delta_tau on the inset and changes by the fixed epsilon_tau times its row evaluation on v_j, while every active sigma inequality vanishing on tau is valid homogeneously on that tangent-cone generator. Tangent-hull equalities are also preserved. Finitely many rows/generators give one positive epsilon_tau. If there are no inactive rows take any fixed positive epsilon_tau.

At y in ri(tau) put xi=z_tau(y)-y in T_tau, ||xi||<=D_tau. Define on each incident cone the convex directional derivative
h_sigma(w)=lim_{t down to0}(f(y+t w)-f(y))/t.
Convex secants give existence, finite upper bounds, positive homogeneity and subadditivity, initially allowing -infinity. Tangent derivatives agree with those of f|tau and obey |h_sigma(xi)|,|h_sigma(-xi)|<=M_tau||xi||. The point z+epsilon_tau v_j is in the SAME incident sigma_j as y. Its gamma difference is bounded by G||xi+epsilon_tau v_j||. Therefore
h_sigma_j(epsilon_tau v_j+xi)<=2C+G(D_tau+epsilon_tau||v_j||).
Subadditivity with -xi gives
h_sigma_j(v_j)<=[2C+(G+M_tau)D_tau]/epsilon_tau+G||v_j||=:U_j.
Choose U_tau>=0 bounding all these numbers and both signed tangent generator costs. This bound is independent of y, including points arbitrarily close to lower faces and points going to infinity. Its derivation never divides by the distance from y to the boundary of tau.

For ANY finite incident direction list with sum w_a=0, sufficiently small endpoints y+t w_a remain in their assigned cells, all incident to tau. The real-endpoint PCC from L0 with equal weights yields sum(f(y+t w_a)-f(y))>=0. If one derivative were -infinity, represent its opposite direction by the fixed generators of L2. Their derivatives have the finite upper bounds just proved, so at small t the zero-sum PCC would have negative total quotient, a contradiction. Thus every incident directional derivative is finite. Passing to the limit proves sum h_sigma_a(w_a)>=0 for EVERY such zero-sum list.

For v in E_tau define H_y(v) as the infimum of the summed finite directional costs over ALL finite decompositions v=sum_a w_a with each w_a in an assigned incident cone; arbitrary nonnegative conic coefficients may be absorbed into the w_a by homogeneity. A fixed-generator representation proves H_y(v)<=K_tau U_tau||v||. For ANY candidate decomposition, append a fixed-generator representation of -v with total coefficient <=K_tau||v||. The zero-sum PCC inequality bounds its cost below by -K_tau U_tau||v||. Thus H_y is finite everywhere, H_y(0)=0, positively homogeneous and subadditive by concatenation, with
-K_tau U_tau||v||<=H_y(v)<=K_tau U_tau||v||.
Both sublinear difference inequalities imply its global Lipschitz continuity. A finite continuous convex full-space function has an affine support at zero: project (0,H_y(0)-t) to its closed epigraph, take a subsequential limiting unit normal, and exclude zero vertical component by the full spatial projection. The touching intercept is zero. Hence there is a linear p_y<=H_y with ||p_y||<=K_tau U_tau. Extend it orthogonally by zero to the original ambient space. For z' in ANY cell sigma incident to tau, convex secants give
f(z')-f(y)>=h_sigma(z'-y)>=H_y(z'-y)>=p_y(z'-y).
This supports the ENTIRE incident cell, not only its small star. It also supports every lower face contained in such a cell. We have obtained a uniformly bounded ambient support on ALL ri(tau), from the face Lipschitz bound and finite geometry, without any assumption of normal independence or that incident cells are complete affine planes.

units.statement: Induction over all faces proves uniform global cellwise Lipschitzness.
units.proof:
Process the finite faces in increasing dimension. At a vertex f|tau is trivially 0-Lipschitz, so L3 constructs its finite uniform supporting bound B_tau=K_tau U_tau. Suppose all proper faces rho of tau already have supports of uniformly bounded norm B_rho which support f on tau whenever y in rho. This holds because tau is contained in an incident top cell of rho. Let B=max_{proper rho}B_rho, using B=0 if there is no boundary, and put M_tau=max(B,G).

On ri(tau), f is finite convex, hence locally Lipschitz and has a finite relative subgradient a at each point q. These facts follow from bounding a cube by its vertex values, reflecting for a lower bound, bounding interior secants, and the same nonvertical full-local epigraph support argument. If a!=0, follow the ray q+t a/||a|| inside the relative affine hull. If it exits tau at a finite t0, its endpoint z lies in a proper face. The subgradient inequality at q and the already available bounded support p_z at z imply
t0||a||<=f(z)-f(q)<=t0 p_z(a/||a||)<=t0 B.
If the ray never exits, bounded difference from the affine gamma on tau gives its limiting secant slope exactly gamma_tau(a/||a||)<=G, and the subgradient inequality implies ||a||<=G. Thus EVERY relative subgradient on ri(tau) has norm <=M_tau. For two interior points, their supporting inequalities give |f(x)-f(z)|<=M_tau||x-z||. Continuous extension to the boundary gives the same estimate for ALL x,z in the closed unbounded tau. This proves its GLOBAL relative-Euclidean Lipschitz bound. Now L3 supplies B_tau uniformly on all ri(tau), allowing the induction to continue.

There are finitely many faces. The recursion M_tau=max(G,max B_rho), B_tau=K_tau U_tau uses only fixed geometry and quantities linear in C,G,M_tau. Induction therefore bounds all M_tau,B_tau by A_X C+B_X G for finite geometry constants. Top-dimensional cells are included. The proof does not require gamma to be rational-affine, does not round its slopes and does not require full-space local convex extensions of f as hypotheses. The actual real weights enter positive spanning, while the geometric constants depend only on the fixed finite carrier and metric.

units.statement: Consequence for working296 and precise remaining original gap.
units.proof:
For the original admitted actual REAL PA PC reference positive on every nonzero cell recession direction, refine once so gamma is affine on each top cell. L4 supplies the previously EXTRA global Euclidean Lipschitz hypothesis of working296 separately on every such closed rational polyhedral cell. The latter single-cell construction can now be considered with its actual affine gamma restriction and a common finite Lipschitz bound: the elementary distance inequality, proper rational-wall auxiliary affine extension, Lipschitz infimal extension/floor, full-affine real-height rational-spatial majorants, finite exact rational contacts and dyadic shifts are its existing reconstructed mechanisms. This is a connection to a whole UNREVIEWED working296 argument, not an automatic acceptance of it or a replacement of gamma on other cells.

The present new theorem is solely Lipschitz control and local ambient supports. It does NOT glue the independently constructed cellwise PA approximants on entire positive-dimensional shared faces, or preserve a common ambient support across all such faces after approximation. Finite contacts alone cannot enforce entire trace equality or compatibility; the whole unreviewed working293 diagnostic and native298 draft demonstrate that issue but are not premises here. Arbitrary several-overlap/complex-face global REAL regularization, the full structural original P05.1 classification, broader compact/literal/abstract categories and non-PA contact sufficiency stay OPEN. No mixed MA is assigned to a nonregularized endpoint by this proof.

The unbalanced-orthant working297 error-floor example does not contradict L4: its boundary tangent star lies in a proper halfspace, so L2 fails. It cannot serve as an original balanced counterexample. Cellwise/intrinsic Lip also cannot be promoted to ambient-distance Lip between nonincident portions or components. No finite tests, build success, proof label or stored hash is a continuum verification or independent acceptance. This full new argument must receive an independent mathematical check before being a grant or a paper acceptance.
